chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn ash-Shah narrated to us, saying: Abu Hamid narrated to us, saying: Abu Yazid narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Salih al-Tamimy narrated to us, on the authority of his father, saying: He narrated to me Anas ibn Muhammad Abu Malik, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ja'far ibn Muhammad, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them all).

He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said, in his will to me: 'O Ali, four things are back-breaking: a leader who disobeys God but is obeyed in his command; a wife whom her husband protects/cares for but she betrays him; poverty for which the owner finds no healer; and a bad neighbor in a place of residence.'

key_terms.قَوَاصِمِ الظَّهْرِ: Back-breaking things (literally: breakers of the back)

ai.seo_question: What are the four back-breaking issues mentioned in the Prophet's will to Ali?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith from the Ahl al-Bayt chain, highlighting these four specific trials as sources of profound spiritual and psychological strain ('qawāsim al-dhahr'). This narration underscores the Shia emphasis on the interplay between social dynamics, such as leadership and neighborly relations, and personal afflictions like poverty and marital discord, framing them as tests of patience (sabr) and fidelity.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 4-24 Muhammad ibn Ali ibn ash-Shah narrated that Abu Hamid quoted Abu Yazid, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Salih al-Tamimy, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Anas ibn Muhammad Abu Malik, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Muhammad as-Sadiq (MGB), on the authority of his father (MGB), on the authority of his grandfather (MGB), on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib (MGB)

that in his will to Ali (MGB) God’s Prophet (MGB) said, “O Ali, four issues are back-breaking: a leader who is obeyed while he disobeys God; a wife who is disloyal to her husband while he is considerate of her; poverty which the poor cannot overcome; and a permanently bad neighbor.”
